D1_gpu: GPU is an NVIDIA RTX 2000 Ada (16 GB, 70 W), not the planned A4500: coupled single-prompt batches use B_CRN = 20 (exp28 used B = 50 multi-prompt for the twin); the engine check therefore tests kernel/batch-shape sensitivity as well as reproduction.
D2_fork_index_rule: The first coded global fork rule (median of the 8 refined per-path fork token indices = 31) landed on a position where all 177 canonical-prefix samples write the same indentation token (token-class MI = 0), which would have made y_v constant by construction. Before any variant state, y_v or commit #1, the rule was replaced by: among the refined per-path indices {14, 30, 32}, the one with the largest token-class mutual information on the canonical prefix (32: 0.62 bits; also the modal refined index). The median-rule output is kept in results/fork_median_rule.json.
D3_forced_paraphrases: The 10 forced paraphrases per mode come from exp9 frozen_prompts.json forced_templates (exp7 prompts_v2.json holds no forced conditions), instantiated with exp8's 6-mode display names.
D4_S10_dropped: S10 (circuit-tracer attribution graph with Gemma Scope 2 transcoders, nnsight backend) was dropped first, as the drop order prescribes, because the slower GPU left no room for the experimental nnsight path; the fallback first-order attribution patching on the four resid_post SAE sites (the S7 output score) is reported and labelled 'first-order attribution, not an attribution graph'.
D5_contrast_batches: Contrast arms (forced, ban, TOP5, TOP5 twin) and sampling validation ran as multi-prompt batches (right-aligned KV); they share the CRN uniforms of the twin's slots, so pairs are coupled through the stream but not bit-coupled through identical batch shapes.
D6_partial_labeller: Fork continuations and sampling validation are labelled by the partial-code labeller (validated 200/200 = 1.00 agreement with the full labeller on S3 T1 valid attempts, U8) and stop at the first decisive evidence or 320 tokens.
D7_permutations: S6a within-template permutation nulls use 200 permutations (T04/R6: 100) with C fixed at 1 inside the permutations, and the S6b readout null uses 300 permutations (minimum attainable p = 0.0033), not 1,000, for time on the slower GPU host.
D8_host_slowdown: Between 07:20 and 08:15 UTC decoding ran at about 600 ms/step instead of 55 ms/step (host contention); it only lengthened the clamp stage (the CRN rows are bit-reproducible per batch shape, so results are unaffected).
D9_das_control: The S9 shuffled-source control permutes templates among forced-BFS sources only, so it still imports a BFS state and is not informative (it moves y as much as DAS); the random-subspace control (about 0) is the informative one. The first DAS run failed (autograd through reused KV buffers) and was re-run with buffers detached per step.
D10_feature_rule_placebo: The pre-registered feature rule (FEAT target-correct >= DiM target-correct with pass >= 0.8 x twin pass) is met by the RANDF placebo at k = 50 at both sites (results/rederive.json), because DiM collapses correctness; the rule is therefore non-discriminating here. The attempted-class (plan shift) McNemar tests are reported as the informative, secondary comparison.
D11_s6c_classifier: S6c uses leave-one-out nearest-class-mean accuracy on z-scored features (a logistic fit on 16k dims did not converge in time, and max-abs scaling collapsed it to the training majority).
D12_not_run: Not run: U4 (clamp readback) and U5 (matched-norm realisation) as separate unit tests (the matched norm is imposed by construction in src/clamp.py and each edit's realised norm is logged per row); the clamp-cell overlay on the S11 generated-position panel; the T04 fork and the T04/R6 cross-prompt readouts (drop order); per-sample displacement at generated tokens 1-32 (prefill displacement at blocks 11-33 is logged).
D13_layer29_spec_nan: The SPEC-site FEAT clamp at layer 29 produced non-finite y in the layer-rule probe; layer 22 (finite, and the better layer at the FORK site) was used for both sites; non-finite sweep rows are counted as n_nonfinite in logit_sweep_summary.json.
